column3: Close to the Hebrew.
NASB adds “for.”
The Hebrew “from it” is rendered “from them.”
“Returned” is rendered “used to pay.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“On that day” is rendered “at that time.”
NASB supplies “word” and “I am.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Went around” is rendered “made a circuit,” and “animals at their feet” as “cattle that followed them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Poured water” is rendered “used to pour water.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“May not” is rendered “No,” and NASB adds “together.”
“Lift up the face” is rendered “regard the presence”; the oath form “if I will look” becomes “I would not look.”
“Musician” is rendered “minstrel,” and “was on him” as “came upon him.”
“Make this wadi ditches, ditches” is rendered “Make this valley full of trenches.”
“Wadi” is rendered “valley,” and “livestock” as “cattle.”
“Moab” is rendered “the Moabites,” and NASB adds “also.”
“Spoil” is rendered “mar.”
“When the offering went up” is rendered “about the time of offering the sacrifice.”
“Every one who girds on a belt and upward” is rendered “all who were able to put on armor and older.”
“Moab” is rendered “the Moabites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The written Hebrew is difficult; NASB renders “they went forward into the land, slaughtering the Moabites.”
NASB adds “only” and “however.” The meaning of “until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth” is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Firstborn” is rendered “oldest son,” and NASB supplies “their own.”
